## Live Simulator tests — Sonnet in Zed only

For now, every live iOS Simulator journey through VisionCapture MCP must use the two existing **Sonnet 5 terminal
sessions in Zed**, one terminal tab per device. Do not spawn Codex live-test agents. Do not use Sol, Terra, Luna,
Fable, Opus, or a Codex `mcp-consumer` to drive the live app unless the owner explicitly replaces this rule.

- Zed tab `customer-1` owns only NestMind Customer 1 and receives this exact one-line prompt:
  `Here is your task, start working on it: /Users/dev-machine/Dev/VisionOS/project-files/active/next-few-days-one-app-plan/customer-1.md`
- Zed tab `customer2` owns only NestMind Customer 2 and receives this exact one-line prompt:
  `Here is your task, start working on it: /Users/dev-machine/Dev/VisionOS/project-files/active/next-few-days-one-app-plan/customer-2.md`
- Send one prompt per tab. Do not add a task ID, expected journey, expected screen, suspected issue, logs, diagnosis,
  hints, or follow-up instructions unless the owner explicitly asks.
- Each Sonnet session must read its own customer file and run the test itself. It must not delegate, spawn an agent,
  use another model, or inspect the other device's task or evidence.
- Start both existing Zed sessions close together when a two-device live test is required. They are independent
  terminal clients and must remain device-locked.
- The coordinator may prepare clean device state and later inspect logs and receipts. The live Sonnet testers do not
  receive coordinator-only context.

This rule supersedes earlier active instructions that used Luna or Terra for live Simulator driving. Luna remains
limited to unit/automation-test code, focused non-live test execution, and saved-evidence work.

### Live-test phone video evidence

The coordinator records each live Simulator journey and prepares a small phone-friendly copy after the run. This is
coordinator work; do not add recording instructions or evidence-processing work to the blind live-test prompt.

- Store phone videos directly under `/Users/dev-machine/Dev/VisionOS/Project-files/videos/`.
- Give every test its own folder using `YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS__App__Device`.
- Use the test's local start time in 24-hour form. Replace spaces with hyphens.
- Name the playable file inside that folder `journey-phone.mp4`.
- Encode it as H.264 with fast start and aim for less than 10 MB so it can open from a phone.
- Keep the full-quality recording in the run's receipt directory. Never overwrite it with the phone copy.

## Git Policy

**FORBIDDEN: Do not commit changes.** Never run `git commit`, `git add`, or create commits unless the user explicitly requests it. Code changes should be made but left uncommitted for the user to review and commit themselves.

## Project Overview

VisionCapture is a macOS app for iOS Simulator automation — screen capture, annotation, workflow learning, and MCP-based automation. Ships as a single Swift package.

The CLI tool (`vision-capture`) is **deprecated**. Keep it in the repo but do not modify unless explicitly asked.

## App-Agnostic Design (Non-Negotiable)

**VisionCapture is an enterprise product.** Companies install it to automate their own iOS apps — apps we've never seen.

- All features MUST work for any iOS app, not just NestMind or any specific app
- Never hardcode app-specific labels, screen names, or navigation assumptions
- Classify UI elements by **standard iOS accessibility roles** (`tab`, `cell`, `button`, `staticText`) — never by specific label text
- Navigation trees, step libraries, and workflows must be built from generic accessibility data
- In docs/examples, use placeholders like `<your.app.bundle.id>`, `[Screen title]` — not real app names

## Skill Compliance (Non-Negotiable)

When the user references a skill — by name, by `/slash-command`, or by describing what it does — **you MUST invoke it via the Skill tool BEFORE doing anything else**. This includes phrases like:
- "use the plan skill", "plan this", "scope this out" → invoke `plan`
- "use the deploy skill", "deploy" → invoke `deploy`
- "use the review skill", "review this" → invoke `review`
- "delegate to codex", "have codex do this" → invoke `codex-delegate`

**Never** absorb a skill's job into your own response. If a skill exists for the task, use it. The skill's instructions override your default behavior. Follow the skill EXACTLY as written — do not skip steps, summarize, or improvise alternatives.

## Coding Rules

- **Accessibility identifiers** — add on all new/modified SwiftUI views. Format: `screen.<feature>.<screen>.root`, `ui.<feature>.<name>Button`. Stable only (no runtime values, array indices, localized strings).
- **Diagrams** — standalone HTML files with embedded Mermaid JS, dark theme (`#0d1117`), color-coded nodes. Never plain markdown mermaid blocks.
- **Performance** — Capture < 1s, UI response < 100ms, Memory < 200MB.
- **Permissions** — Screen Recording (`NSScreenCaptureUsageDescription`), Accessibility (global hotkey).

## Task Handling — Sol, Terra, and Luna

The project uses one decision owner and two implementation-support roles. The current role model is authoritative in
`Project-files/adr/0013-separate-lead-terra-implementation-and-luna-quality.md`; the old dual-team documents are
historical reference only.

| Role | Model | Owns | Does not own |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Sol technical lead** | GPT-5.6 Sol, high | Every product and architecture decision, task briefs, review, and final acceptance | Production code and tests |
| **Terra senior developer** | GPT-5.6 Terra, high | Production implementation from an approved Sol brief | Product, architecture, public-contract, and test-strategy decisions; tests |
| **Luna routine worker** | GPT-5.6 Luna, low | File reading, search, evidence, inventories, mechanical work | Product and architecture decisions; production behavior |
| **Luna unit-test engineer** | GPT-5.6 Luna, low | Unit and automation tests, focused test execution, coverage evidence | Production behavior decisions |

Every production change follows this path:

```text
Sol decision and bounded brief -> Terra production code -> Luna tests and evidence -> Sol review and acceptance
```

No role may silently invent missing behavior. Do not use the historical `codex-dev`, `codex-quality`, or
`codex-scout` labels for new work.

The table above governs implementation support. It does not authorize any Codex role to drive live Simulator tests;
the active Sonnet-in-Zed rule above owns live-test routing.

# Tracker: Live Notch Acceptance

Goal: the Live Notch feature clears every remaining acceptance gate - the driver drives managed devices, the
managed route is proven and accepted, preview-only is real, the caller skill documents all three modes, three full
live journeys pass, learned knowledge survives a run, a recorded run starts in the right order, native iOS popups
are clickable headless on managed clones, a cold-start recording answers its caller before the client times out,
and the notch HUD and proof video show a clean, full picture.

Details, scope, code, evidence: [implementation-live-notch-acceptance-2026-08-17.md](./implementation-live-notch-acceptance-2026-08-17.md)

The recorder feature itself is already closed - see
[tracker-live-notch-work-2026-08-15.md](../live-notch-work/tracker-live-notch-work-2026-08-15.md). This tracker does
not reopen it.

# Task 10.8 — the anchor rule, and the owner's four rulings

Date: 2026-08-19. Base: the deployed 10.1 + 10.2-10.7 tree.
Not done here, by rule: no deploy, no commit, no app run, no test files, nothing under `Tests/` or
`Package.swift`.

Files touched (four):

- `Sources/UI/Components/ProofActivityHUDContent.swift` — minimum card width, feed envelope
- `Sources/UI/Components/SimulatorFrameLiveTile.swift` — run-stage line position
- `Sources/App/NotchComposite/NotchCompositeLayout.swift` — feed text size in the video
- `Sources/App/NotchComposite/NotchCompositeFeedView.swift` — row budget for the smaller text

## Ruling 1 — the run-stage line moves below the preview

The line used to sit between the header and the preview, which meant a *running* recording still pushed the
preview down by the one thing the four removals had not cleared. It is now its own view below the preview
tile (`SimulatorFrameLiveTile.swift`, `runLifecycleStageLine`), using space that was already free.

With it gone from that band, `previewControls` is gated purely on the four display switches
(`showsAnyPreviewChrome`), all of which are off — so the band emits nothing at all and **the preview sits hard
under the header unconditionally, run or no run.** That is the ruling, exactly.

The line keeps its behaviour and its accessibility identifier (`…simulatorPreview.lifecycleStage`): present
only while a recorded run is publishing real stages, absent otherwise rather than blank or stale.

## Ruling 2 — the feed's empty space stays empty

No code. Nothing was added to fill leftover room, and the intent is now written where a future reader will
meet it, on `rowsArea(maxViewportHeight:)`: *"Nothing is ever added to fill leftover room. Owner ruling,
2026-08-19: 'empty is honest' — rows fill from the top and whatever is left stays black."*

My earlier measurement stands recorded beside the ruling rather than against it: on a full run the rows still
ended about three quarters down the column. Ruling 3 shrinks that naturally by fitting about half as many rows
again in the same space — which is what the coordinator predicted when the ruling was given.

## Ruling 3 — the feed text is smaller, and the size was picked by looking, not by taste

`NotchCompositeLayout.feedRenderScale` 3 → 2, and `feedPointWidth` 460 → 500 (feed column 1380 → 1000
pixels). Canvas goes from **2586 x 2622 to 2206 x 2622**; the device half is unchanged at 1206 and now takes
55 % of the frame instead of 47 %.

Lowering the scale lays the same views out in a larger point box for the same pixels, so text shrinks within
its column and more rows fit: feed text drops from 39 to 26 video pixels (**one third smaller**) and the
column goes from about 27 rows of capacity to about 41.

**The phone-readability check the owner asked for, done on a real frame — both images are in this folder.**

1. Extracted a full-resolution frame from the actual recorded video (`2586 x 2622`, the 12:03 run).
2. Simulated the proposed sizing on it exactly: the feed half scaled by 2/3 — the true glyph-size change —
   and placed in a 1000-pixel column beside the untouched device half, giving the real 2206 x 2622 canvas.
3. Scaled both the current and the proposed frame to **1170 pixels wide**, an iPhone's screen width.
4. Read both myself.

`phone-width-BEFORE-scale3.png` — current. The feed text is the same size as the app's own *title* text and
larger than the app's subtitle. That is the imbalance the owner meant by "why is the text so big".

`phone-width-AFTER-scale2.png` — proposed. Every feed row is still clearly legible: the stage ladder, the
driver rows, and the full body of the `APP_NOT_INSTALLED` refusal card. And the feed text now sits at roughly
the size of the app's own secondary body text ("Your digital knowledge companion") in the same frame.

That last sentence is the calibration, and it is why this number rather than a smaller one: **the feed is
readable exactly as well as the recorded app's own body text is, at the same viewing size.** If a viewer can
read the app in the video, they can read the feed beside it. Going further would have put the feed below the
app it is describing, which is the floor the owner set.

Honest limit of the simulation: it reproduces glyph size exactly, but not the extra rows or the different line
wrapping the real renderer will produce at the new column width. Legibility — the question being asked — is
what it answers.

## Ruling 4 — the card can no longer be persisted narrow enough to squeeze the feed

`minCardWidth` 560 → **640**, and it is now derived rather than chosen:

```
minCardWidth = simulatorTileWidth * 2 + contentHorizontalInset * 2 + simulatorTileToRowsGap
             = 294 * 2 + 18 * 2 + 16
             = 640
```

That is the width at which **the feed is exactly as wide as the device preview beside it** — the feed's
working floor under the anchor rule. The preview is the anchor and the feed is the other half of the same
picture; once the feed is narrower than the phone, it is the feed's prose, not the phone, that stops being
readable first.

At the old 560 the feed would have been 214 points after 10.7 widened the tile to 294. Deriving the minimum
means a later tile change can never quietly reopen that. A width already persisted below 640 is raised to it
on read by the presenter's existing clamp (`ProofActivityHUDPresenter.swift:363`), so no user is left in the
bad state.

Feed width by card width, after this change: 640 → 294 (floor), 720 default → 374, 820 max → 474.

## The anchor rule itself

*The notch's height targets the preview's height; everything else fits inside that envelope; the freed space
is absorbed by the preview and the feed growing, and nothing new is added.*

The one place this was not true was the feed. It was capped at `maxViewportHeight` = 340 points, a number that
suited a notch with no preview in it — so beside a 640-point preview it left most of the column unused and the
"feed grows" half of the rule unimplemented.

The feed now takes its cap from its caller (`rowsArea(maxViewportHeight:)`), and there are exactly two
callers, which *are* the rule:

- beside a mounted preview → `previewAnchoredViewportHeight` (640, the preview's own height);
- on its own → `maxViewportHeight` (340, unchanged, so ordinary automation behaves exactly as before).

The preview-mounted cap is deliberately the tile height and **not** the tile column height. The column is the
header plus the tile plus the stage line, so capping the feed at the tile alone is what guarantees the feed can
never be the element that makes the notch taller than the preview envelope. Everything else in the card
(status strip, footer, insets) is fixed and small, so with the feed bounded the preview is the only thing that
sets the height — which is the rule, enforced rather than hoped for.

## Build

See `build.txt`. `swiftformat --lint` and `swiftlint` clean on all four touched files (`lint.txt`).

## What a live look still has to confirm

- the preview really does sit flush under the header during a run, with the stage line below it;
- the feed really does fill the taller envelope;
- the recorded video's feed text reads as balanced against the phone at full size — the check above was on a
  simulated frame, so the real renderer's output still has to be seen;
- a card previously persisted below 640 comes back clamped rather than stuck.

---

# Addendum — the `no_device_frame` regression, root-caused and fixed

Date: 2026-08-19, after the 12:44 deploy. Symptom: both recording starts failed instantly
(728 ms, then 154 ms) with `NOTCH_RECORDER_START_FAILED`, `paired_operation_started:false`, and both
state markers naming `reason:"no_device_frame"`. Full trace: `showcase-journal.md`.

## The hypothesis I was given, and what I found instead

The suggested cause was that 10.8's reflow or gating changed when the preview tile mounts, so the recorder
started before a frame source existed. **That is not it, and the tile is not involved at all.** The recorder
reads the presentation mailbox directly; it never goes through the tile, and the tile only ever reads that
mailbox too (`SimulatorFrameLiveTile.swift`, the surface view's display-link coordinator). Nothing in the
10.8 diff touches frame delivery.

**The defect is mine, and it is from 10.1, not 10.8.** It is an ordering hazard that 10.8 only changed the
timing of.

## The actual sequence

The run's start steps execute in this order (`LiveNotchRecordingProductionRuntime.performClaimedStep`):

```
  bindDeviceAndDisplay      -> transport starts; frames begin arriving
  applySettingsSnapshot
  presentFixedNotchLayout   -> mailbox.begin(...)  ** CLEARS THE MAILBOX FRAME **
  deliverFirstIdentityValidFrame
  freezeExactNotchWindow
  confirmRecorderWriterStart -> my recorder read the mailbox ONCE and refused
```

Two facts make that fatal together:

1. `prepareSimulatorPreview` calls `simulatorPreviewMailbox.begin(...)`
   (`ProofActivityHUDPresenter.swift:162`), and `begin` publishes state `.starting` **with a nil frame** —
   deliberately, so the notch never opens showing a previous run's picture.
2. `deliverFirstIdentityValidFrame` proves the **transport** has a frame, not the mailbox. It returns as soon
   as `phase == .streaming`, `latestFrameSequence > 0` and the transport's own `currentFrame != nil`
   (`SimulatorFrameTransportAwaiting.swift:32-35`) — all of which can already be true from frames that
   arrived *before* the mailbox was cleared.

So when any frame had arrived before the notch was presented, that wait is satisfied by state the transport
already held, returns on its first loop iteration, and the mailbox is still empty. The only thing between the
clear and the next `publish` (`SimulatorFrameTransportActorMessages.swift:116`) is one frame interval — and
my `start` read the mailbox exactly once and refused. Hence an instant, repeatable `no_device_frame`.

That also explains why 12:03 passed and 12:44 did not, without either build being "the bug": on the earlier
run the first frame happened to arrive *after* the notch was presented, so the clear removed nothing and the
frame that ended the wait was the one that populated the mailbox. It was a race the whole time. My original
`start` assumed the lifecycle's first-frame guarantee applied to the mailbox. It never did.

**Recorded honestly:** I could not confirm the timing shift from logs — the runtime's stage lines are
`Logger.info`, which the unified log does not persist, so `log show` returned nothing for the failure window.
The ordering hazard above is established from the code and fully explains both the failure and the earlier
success; the specific timing tip is inferred, not observed.

## The fix

`LiveNotchPaintedCompositeRecorder.start` now waits, bounded, for the mailbox to carry a frame
(`awaitFirstDeviceFrame()`), instead of reading once and refusing. Budget 10 seconds — comfortably inside the
run's own 30-second start deadline, so a genuinely dead stream still fails the step rather than hanging it,
while a mailbox that is one frame interval behind simply succeeds.

This removes the race rather than re-tuning it. The recorder now asks for what it actually needs — a frame in
the mailbox it samples from — instead of inferring it from a guarantee that was about something else. The
reasoning is written above the function so the wait is not later "simplified" back into a single read.

Two log lines were added for the next run: `notchComposite stage=firstFrame result=ready waited=true` when
the wait was genuinely needed, and `result=timedOut` if the budget is ever exhausted.

**Nothing in the 10.8 slice was reverted.** All four rulings and the anchor rule stand exactly as accepted.

## Build

See `build-no-device-frame-fix.txt`. `swiftformat --lint` and `swiftlint` clean on the touched file.

## Not established

The fix is reasoned from a fully traced cause, not yet observed. The next recording start proves it. If
`waited=true` appears in the log, that is the race being caught and survived rather than lost.

---

# Addendum 2 — after the fix: the stream really is dead, and it is device-side

Date: 2026-08-19, after the 13:01 deploy. My `no_device_frame` fix behaved exactly as designed and turned a
misdiagnosis into a measurement: recording `3e38e9e3` waited the full 10 seconds and then failed honestly.

The decisive evidence is the **helper's** own log, which — unlike the app's `Logger.info` lines — the unified
log does persist. Every recording start today, one row each:

| Local time | Run | `callbacksSeen` | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12:00:14 | the good reproof run | **2659** | healthy, streamed until 12:03:44 |
| 12:46:49 | showcase attempt 1 | **0** | failed 179 ms |
| 12:47:45 | showcase attempt 2 | **0** | failed 56 ms |
| 12:55:58 | a further attempt | **0** | failed 51 ms |
| 13:03:04 | first run after my fix | **0** | failed after the full 10 s wait |

`callbacksSeen` is the number of frame callbacks the simulator's framebuffer service actually delivered.
**Since 12:03:44 it has been zero, every time.**

The full terminal line from the post-fix run:

```
frameStreamSourceGraph          phase=acquired
frameStreamCallbackRegistration returned=1
frameStreamInitialSnapshotAdmission admitted=1
frameStreamTerminal reason=-1 firstSurfacesSnapshotSeen=1 firstPropertiesSnapshotSeen=0 \
                   callbacksSeen=0 callbacksAdmitted=1 callbackRegistered=1
frameStreamSourceGraph          phase=released
```

The helper acquires the source graph, registers its callback **successfully**, admits the initial snapshot —
and then the device never calls back, not once, in ten seconds. Then it releases cleanly.

(`firstPropertiesSnapshotSeen=0` is not the discriminator: the healthy 12:00 run has it too. `callbacksSeen`
is.)

## The wedge hypothesis is refuted, three ways over

The suggestion was that the crashed 12:47 starts left the single-surface invariant wedged, with every new
stream waiting on an acknowledgement that will never come. It cannot be that:

1. **`surfaceOwner` is per-run.** It is a stored property of `SimulatorFrameTransportActor`
   (`SimulatorFrameTransportActor.swift:57`), and a brand-new transport actor is constructed for every
   recording in `launchHelper` (`LiveNotchRecordingProductionRuntimeStart.swift:63-70`). No instance outlives
   its run.
2. **Both processes are newer than the failure.** The app is pid 10786 (started 13:01) and the helper is pid
   11474, *spawned by launchd at 13:03:03 for this very run* — the helper pid changed on every attempt
   (92431 → 4720 → 11474). The condition survived all of that, so it cannot live in either process.
3. **The helper's own log shows nothing was held.** `phase=acquired` → `phase=released`, with zero surfaces
   ever mapped. There is no stuck acknowledgement, because there was never a surface to acknowledge.

So there is nothing to un-wedge app-side, and no app-side recovery path is possible or needed — the app is
already doing the right thing and reporting it honestly.

## Ruling: the recovery is a clone reboot

The stuck state is on the clone's side of the transport: its framebuffer service accepts a callback
registration and then never fires it. Shutdown + boot of `10A4F537` restarts exactly that layer, and it is the
only lever that reaches it. The identity probe still works perfectly (screen 1 enumerated as 1206 x 2622), so
the device is reachable — it is specifically frame delivery that has stopped.

**Go/no-go after the reboot:** the next run's helper line should show `callbacksSeen` climbing into the
thousands, as the healthy 12:00 run did. Zero again would mean the fault is deeper than the clone.

## Correction to one reported fact

The notch showing **NO SIGNAL** at ~12:47 is not evidence of a dead stream. That label is driven by
`ProofActivityHUDModel.signalState`, which is derived from `lastEventAt` — the last **proof event** — against
a 30-second threshold (`ProofActivityHUDView.swift`, `ProofActivityHUDMetrics.noSignalSeconds`). It means "no
automation activity for 30 seconds", not "no frames". The helper log evidences the dead stream independently
and dates its onset between 12:03:44 and 12:46:49.

## Discovered consequence of task 10.5 — recorded, not a reversal request

The indicator that *would* have shown this on screen is the preview state badge — `STREAM UNAVAILABLE` /
`LIVE · STATIC` — which is the element the owner ruled hidden in 10.5. The stated and accepted cost was that a
frozen stream becomes indistinguishable from an idle app. This incident shows the same blindness covers a
stream that never starts: the notch looked ordinary while no frame had arrived for forty minutes.

His ruling stands and nothing here asks to change it. Recording it so the trade is visible with a real
incident behind it rather than only as a predicted cost.

---

# Addendum 3 — the two-layer "contradiction" explained, our builds exonerated, and the next lever

Date: 2026-08-19, after the clone reboot also failed.

## (a) `firstFrame=true` and `callbacksSeen=0` do not contradict each other

They count different things, and the source says so plainly.

`callbacksSeen` is incremented in exactly one place — `handleFrameCallbackForToken:`
(`Sources/SimulatorFramePrivateAdapter/SimulatorFramePrivateStreamAdmission.m:12-16`), which runs only when the
simulator's framebuffer service fires its frame callback.

But that is not the only way a frame is admitted. `admitInitialSurfaceSnapshotForToken:` (`:18-21`) admits one
frame with origin `InitialSurfaceSnapshot`, at registration time, **without touching `callbacksSeen`**. That
is the `frameStreamInitialSnapshotAdmission admitted=1` line, and it is why the terminal line reads
`callbacksAdmitted=1` while `callbacksSeen=0`: one frame was admitted, zero callbacks produced it.

So both layers are telling the truth:

- the app's `firstFrame=true` means **one** frame reached it — the initial snapshot;
- the helper's `callbacksSeen=0` means **no frame after that one has ever existed**.

## And that closes the whole causal chain

1. The helper registers and admits exactly one frame, the initial surface snapshot. The app receives it:
   `latestFrameSequence` becomes 1, `currentFrame` is set, and the mailbox is published to.
2. `presentFixedNotchLayout` runs and calls `mailbox.begin(...)`, which **clears that one frame**
   (`ProofActivityHUDPresenter.swift:162`).
3. `deliverFirstIdentityValidFrame` is satisfied instantly, because it reads the transport's own retained
   `currentFrame` — the snapshot — not the mailbox.
4. The recorder then waits its full ten seconds for a mailbox frame. None ever comes, because the only frame
   that ever existed was cleared in step 2 and no callback will produce another.
5. The terminal diagnostic prints `firstFrame=true` beside the helper's `callbacksSeen=0`.

Every observation fits, in both directions: it also explains why the healthy 12:00 run was fine — 2659
callbacks kept re-publishing to the mailbox, so step 2 cleared a frame that was immediately replaced.

**One product note worth recording.** In this exact state the old screen-capture recorder would have produced
a video that *looked* normal — it filmed the notch, and the notch would have shown that one still frame
frozen for the whole run. The painted recorder refuses instead. A silent frozen-device video is worse than a
loud failure on a proof surface, so this is the painter behaving better than what it replaced, in a case
nobody designed for.

## (b) Our 12:44+ builds did not change what the helper registers for

I diffed the helper's full registration sequence between the healthy 12:00 run and the failed 13:03 run. It is
**identical line for line**, apart from the request UUID:

```
identityProbeStage stage=enumerationSent / enumerationCallback
screenMetadata site=accepted side=port       screenID=2 uniqueIdLength=11 pixelWidth=720  pixelHeight=480  screenType=1 displayClass=1
screenMetadata site=accepted side=port       screenID=1 uniqueIdLength=10 pixelWidth=1206 pixelHeight=2622 screenType=0 displayClass=0
screenMetadata site=accepted side=enumerated screenID=1 uniqueIdLength=10 pixelWidth=1206 pixelHeight=2622 screenType=0 displayClass=0
screenMetadata site=accepted side=enumerated screenID=2 uniqueIdLength=11 pixelWidth=720  pixelHeight=480  screenType=1 displayClass=1
identityTerminal reason=0 identityPresent=1 descriptorPresent=1
frameStreamCompleteIdentity reason=0 identityPresent=1 descriptorPresent=1 alreadyTerminal=0
frameStreamSourceGraph phase=acquired
frameStreamCallbackRegistration returned=1
frameStreamInitialSnapshotAdmission admitted=1
```

Same screens, same port and enumerated sides, same dimensions, same screen types and display classes, same
acquire, same successful registration. **The registration is byte-identical and the service simply stopped
calling back.**

That is consistent with the code: nothing in the 10.8 diff reaches the helper at all, and the Native Device
mode 10.1 introduced was already in force during the healthy 12:00 run, so it is exonerated too. The 12:44
deploy sitting inside the failure window is a coincidence of timing, not a cause.

## (c) Ruling on restarting CoreSimulatorService: not yet — run the free discriminator first

The elimination so far is genuinely strong: fresh helper process every run, two fresh app processes, and a
clone reboot, none of which changed anything, with identical registration throughout. That does point at the
host-side service as the only surviving layer.

But a `CoreSimulatorService` restart takes down **every** booted simulator, including the DO-NOT-TOUCH ones,
and it would be spent on a hypothesis we have not tested. There is a test that costs one recording start:

**Start a recording against the other managed clone in set `07b6c892`.**

- If it also reports `callbacksSeen=0`, the fault is host-wide, `CoreSimulatorService` is implicated properly,
  and the restart is justified — as the owner's decision, with its full collateral stated.
- If it streams normally (`callbacksSeen` in the thousands), the fault is bound to this one clone. A reboot
  already failed to clear it, which would point at that device's record inside the service rather than the
  service itself — and re-provisioning the clone is far cheaper than restarting everything.

Those two outcomes lead to genuinely different remedies, which is what makes the test worth doing before the
blunt instrument. Note the identity probe still enumerates this clone's screens perfectly, so
`CoreSimulatorService` is responding — it is specifically frame-callback delivery that has stopped, which is
exactly the discrimination the second clone would settle.

# Addendum 4 — the service-restart run never reached the frame stream (verified)

Date: 2026-08-19, ~14:07.

The 13:57 start (after the `CoreSimulatorService` restart and full simulator reboots) wedged in driver setup
and produced no run directory. Checked whether it nonetheless got far enough to answer the frame question:

```
log show --predicate 'subsystem CONTAINS "FramebufferHelper"' --start "2026-08-19 13:40:00" --info --debug
  -> 0 lines
```

**Zero helper activity of any kind after 13:40.** The frame helper was never started, so there was no identity
probe, no source graph, no callback registration and no `frameStreamTerminal` line.

This matters for how the specimen is read later: the service restart's effect on frame delivery is
**completely unknown**, not "tested and it still failed". Nothing about specimen 3 is evidence either way on
the frame pipe. The last and only frame-stage evidence remains the 13:26 run's `callbacksSeen=0`, which was
taken *before* the service restart.

## Why it could not answer — and the design input that falls out of it

The run's stage ladder puts driver setup upstream of the frame stream. In order:

```
Preparing the device -> Installing the driver app -> Checking recording settings ->
Checking developer tools -> Starting the frame helper -> Connecting the device display ->
Applying preview settings -> Opening the notch -> Waiting for the first frame ->
Locking the notch window -> Starting the recorder -> Ready
```

So **anything that wedges in driver setup makes the frame pipe unobservable**, even though the two have
nothing to do with each other: the device's display was enumerable the whole time. Today that cost us the one
measurement we most wanted, twice.

Concrete input for Phase 9, grounded in this: the frame stream's health does not depend on the driver being
installed, so proving it should not be gated behind that. Either the frame helper starts earlier in the
ladder, or there is a standalone frame probe — attach, count callbacks for a second, detach — that a caller
or an operator can run without starting a recording at all. Either shape would have answered today's question
in seconds instead of never, and would also give the product the early "this device is not sending pictures"
signal that Discovered work already wants.

# ADR 0050: Use a Supervised Exact-UDID Simulator Framebuffer Helper and Record Only the Activity Notch

## Status

Accepted

## Date

2026-08-14

## Context

VisionCapture needs one phone-friendly visual record of a live Simulator test. The record must show the real selected
Simulator beside the real activity and proof rows already rendered in the activity notch. It must work when the
selected Simulator has a visible Simulator.app window and when Simulator.app shows no window for that device.

Public Apple tooling can take screenshots and record a device video, but it does not expose the required continuous
in-memory display stream. ScreenCaptureKit can record the VisionCapture notch window, but it cannot supply a
no-window Simulator framebuffer. The needed source is therefore a compatibility-sensitive private
CoreSimulator/SimulatorKit route.

This decision is hard to reverse because it creates a private-framework boundary, a bundled process, an XPC protocol,
a public MCP contract, persisted consent, a durable output shape, and release-package obligations. It would also be
surprising if future work moved private selectors into the main app, recorded a second Simulator file, silently
changed devices, or let preview work delay MCP actions.

The current branch contains the activity notch and its operation-ID proof merge. Gate 1's contained signed XPC helper,
closed transport/provenance checks, helper package resources, and assembly/probe seams are implemented and
source-approved. Gate 2's helper-only private adapter and exact-UDID integrated/Internal-display identity source gate are
also implemented and source-approved. Gate 2 live Simulator evidence is still pending and is not accepted at the
product gate.

The public live-test recording object, recording coordinator, exact-notch recorder, preview settings, Gate 3 frame
callback/IOSurface transport, preview UI, and notch-recording integration remain **planned, not implemented**.

ADRs 0045 through 0049 were accepted on the earlier recording branch but are not files in this branch. Their retained
rules are restated here so this ADR has no dangling local links. The frozen reference is recording-branch commit:

```text
e8c329db56f1429e43a7137cb463d34296506f3b
```

That earlier design recorded one notch video plus one Simulator video for every requested UDID. This decision replaces
that media shape and its multi-device recording model. It retains the useful lifecycle, wire separation, output
durability, privacy, performance-isolation, activity-pulse, and bounded-finalization rules where they are compatible
with one device and one video.

The owner-approved source specification is
[Single-Device Live Simulator in Recorded Notch](../active/live-notch-work/specification/spec-single-device-live-simulator-in-recorded-notch-2026-08-14.md).

## Decision

For one explicitly requested recording run, VisionCapture binds one immutable exact Simulator UDID, streams that
device's unique integrated/Internal non-CarPlay display through one supervised bundled XPC helper, renders the live
pixels inside the existing activity notch, and records only that exact notch window to one H.264 MP4.

The device stream is live in-memory presentation. It is not a source recording. The only pixel-bearing media output is:

```text
<run-directory>/notch__journey.mp4
```

There is no provider choice, replacement provider, retry/reconnect, device substitution, screenshot polling,
Simulator video, post-run merge, network stream, or fallback.

### Relationship to ADR 0024

[ADR 0024](./0024-use-mode-specific-execution-for-visible-and-headless-computer-use.md) remains accepted and
unchanged. It chooses input transport: exact-window input for visible Computer Use and the driver lane for headless
actions. This ADR chooses only the visual preview source and notch-recording path. Preview never selects an action
transport, never changes caller authority, and never changes WDA, proof, OCR, Accessibility, cache, or Interaction
Truth.

"No-window" means Simulator.app does not need to show or own a window for the selected device. A logged-in graphical
macOS session and WindowServer are still required because VisionCapture must render and record the notch.

### One immutable exact UDID

- `recording.command=start` accepts `udids` with exactly one non-empty exact Simulator UDID.
- Zero entries or more than one entry is malformed and rejects before a run ID or side effect.
- The trimmed UDID is copied into immutable run identity.
- The helper binds only that exact UDID. It never uses a device name, `booted`, the first device, the largest surface,
  or another convenient candidate.
- A second start while a run is non-terminal returns `RECORDING_CONFLICT`. It creates no run and leaks no active ID.
- Continue, stop, and cancel require the matching opaque recording ID.

### Public MCP recording contract V2

The current branch has no public recording wire. V2 is introduced selectively; it is not a runtime migration from a
shipped V1 on this branch.

VisionCapture keeps one public MCP tool, `execute`. It adds an optional closed top-level `recording` object:

```json
{
  "schema_version": 2,
  "command": "start | continue | stop | cancel",
  "recording_id": "<required canonical UUID for continue/stop/cancel>",
  "udids": ["<exactly-one-simulator-udid-for-start>"]
}
```

The retained request rules are:

- `start` requires `udids` and forbids `recording_id`.
- `continue`, `stop`, and `cancel` require `recording_id` and forbid `udids`.
- `start` and `continue` may accompany a normal operation. The normal operation's `parameters.udid` must equal the
  selected recording UDID.
- `stop` and `cancel` are allowed only on the control-only request `manage recording`.
- Control-only recording requests forbid `bundle_id`, `mode`, `parameters`, and `session_id`.
- The destination, helper, provider, preview size, and FPS never appear on the wire.
- Unknown fields, wrong types, unsupported schema versions, invalid command combinations, and zero/multiple UDIDs use
  JSON-RPC `-32602` before action IDs, proof events, device I/O, run allocation, helper launch, or file work.
- `RECORDING_UDIDS_REQUIRED` means a missing or empty start array.
- `RECORDING_UDID_INVALID` includes a non-string, blank, duplicate, or more-than-one start member.
- A normal-operation UDID mismatch uses `RECORDING_ACTION_UDID_MISMATCH` before either run or action side effects.
- When `recording` is omitted, response shape and action behaviour remain unchanged and no recording field is added.

A syntactically valid recording command result publishes one top-level `recording` object and one byte-equivalent
model-visible content block. Its `schema_version` is `2`. The retained fields are `command`, `accepted`, optional
`recording_id`, optional `state`, one-element `requested_udids`, `elapsed_ms`, `has_known_failure`, normal-branch
`paired_operation_started`, normal-branch `paired_operation_outcome`, optional `reason_code`, optional `message`,
optional `run_directory`, and terminal `videos`.

#### Amendment 2026-08-18 — `paired_operation_outcome` and the timeout code boundary

Additive V2 amendment. `schema_version` stays `2`; no field is removed, renamed, or given a new meaning.

`paired_operation_outcome` is **action status, not recording status**. It answers "did the paired normal operation
work?", which no recording field ever answered and which `accepted`, `state`, and `has_known_failure` must not be read
as answering.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `not_started` | The normal-operation pipeline was not entered. Always published with `paired_operation_started: false`. |
| `succeeded` | It was entered and the final action result has `isError != true`. Always with `paired_operation_started: true`. |

### Closed lifecycle and ordering

The one-active-run states remain:

```text
starting -> recording -> finalizing -> completed | incomplete | cancelled | failed
```

`starting` and `finalizing` each have one 30-second whole-phase deadline. The 10-minute client inactivity lease runs
only while `recording`. Terminal state never reopens. A later run gets a new recording ID and a new stream generation.

Start order is exact:

1. Validate the closed V2 request and exactly one UDID.
2. Read persisted consent. Unless it is explicitly valid and true, reject before a run or side effect.
3. Create immutable run identity, claim the single active slot, and enter `starting`.
4. Validate destination and closed persisted preview settings.
5. Resolve active canonical DeveloperDir and its exact accepted Xcode build.
6. Validate and launch the bundled helper.
7. Bind the exact booted device generation and exactly one integrated/Internal non-CarPlay display with an exact
   screen identity.
8. Apply the settings snapshot.
9. Present the fixed final notch layout.
10. Deliver and display one identity-valid frame.
11. Freeze the exact notch window geometry and resolve its exact `CGWindowID`.
12. Start the exact-window ScreenCaptureKit recorder and await writer-start confirmation.
13. Enter `recording`, show REC and elapsed time, then invoke the paired normal operation.

No paired operation follows a failure in steps 1 through 12.

Stop order is exact:

1. Enter `finalizing`; hide REC/timer, disable preview settings, and keep the fixed preview/rows mounted.
2. Finalize the exact-notch recorder once within the remaining 30-second phase budget.
3. Stop/invalidate the helper connection once; release mapped surfaces and fence late messages.
4. Validate the one non-empty playable H.264 MP4.
5. Persist terminal truth, restore normal HUD presentation, and release the active slot.

`completed` requires a clean explicit stop or accepted clean idle finalization, a valid notch MP4, and no irreversible
source, destination, recorder, marker, or deadline failure. Cancel and cooperative shutdown end `cancelled`. A crash
during `starting` reconciles `failed`; a crash during `recording` or `finalizing` reconciles `incomplete`. Recovery
never promotes bytes to `completed` and never resumes a run.

### Activity, idle finalization, and hard isolation

Retained activity rules are reduced to the one selected UDID:

- A matching normal operation emits internal `began` immediately before its existing app pipeline and exactly one
  `ended` on return or throw.
- Pulses contain only run ID, exact UDID, monotonic time, and phase. They contain no pixels or customer vocabulary.
- Pulse bookkeeping is enqueue-only. The action path never awaits preview, helper, encode, file, timer, or finalization.
- The device becomes idle-eligible only with zero in-flight actions and 20 seconds since its latest qualifying pulse.
- When it is idle-eligible, all in-flight counts are zero, and 60 continuous seconds pass without device or run-scoped
  notch activity, Core uses the same bounded finalization and validation as explicit stop.
- A successful run-only preview setting update is run-scoped notch activity. Frames and heartbeats are not.
- The 10-minute client lease remains the emergency bound. It ends `incomplete`, not `completed`.
- One coordinator-owned monotonic reaper is used. No per-request polling task and no global MCP lane serialization.

Pixels and preview health bypass HTTPServer/MCP, ProofEventStream, action/proof lanes, WDA/Interaction, OCR,
Accessibility, screenshots, Discovery Cache, and workflow truth. Only start preflight may gate the paired operation.
After `recording`, preview work cannot cancel, retry, delay, upgrade, or downgrade any action or proof result.

All private framework loading, private class/selector calls, display discovery, framebuffer callbacks, raw-surface
ownership, scaling, and drop policy live in one bundled XPC helper. The main app does not load CoreSimulator or
SimulatorKit for this feature. CaptureCore remains free of private APIs and external package dependencies.

Inside that helper, the Objective-C `SimulatorFramePrivateAdapter` target owns the private display object, raw
Simulator callbacks, `framebufferSurface`, raw IOSurface lock/seed/copy/unlock, the exact three-slot owned ring,
scaling, and callback-side dropping. Its public header exposes only VisionCapture-owned identity/configuration/frame-
lease values, a typed VisionCapture event sink, and the public `xpc_object_t` made by
`IOSurfaceCreateXPCObject`. It exposes no `IOSurfaceRef`, base address, `void *`, private object/protocol/selector,
private framework header, or Apple's raw callback block. The Swift helper owns the closed XPC session, generations,
wire frame sequence, newest-notification state, heartbeat, and release-ack routing. The app owns
`IOSurfaceLookupFromXPCObject`, at most one mapped current surface, and acknowledgement only after every app mapping,
image/texture, presentation, and GPU use has released that surface.

The adapter has one serial utility-QoS state queue as the sole owner of every mutable private/callback/ring/token/
terminal fact and one separate serial utility-QoS copy queue. The state queue reserves one free slot and fixes its
tokens, the copy queue performs only the reserved lock/copy/unlock, and the state queue revalidates before publish or
release. There is at most one copy plus one replaceable newest raw candidate. There are no synchronous cross-queue
waits, callback-sized task growth, or multiple terminal drains.

The public Objective-C configuration value has one designated full initializer; plain `init` and `new` are
unavailable. Initial configuration, requested-setting application, and automatic source reconfiguration use separate
typed callbacks. Every requested-setting or automatic-source applied callback carries one positive, monotonic,
never-reused request token. Token, lease, source-ordinal, generation, revision, sequence, and counter overflow is
terminal before mutation; none wraps.

Objective-C failure enums contain only adapter-observable private identity/ABI, callback, surface, copy/allocation,
configuration/scratch, and adapter-overflow facts. Swift owns and maps all V3/session protocol, acknowledgement,
deadline, handshake, precedence, XPC send, update/source/terminal timeout, supersession, and cancellation reasons.
No wire enum or session state enters the adapter header.

The transport uses Apple's modern Swift XPC API (`XPCSession` / `XPCListener`), not an `NSXPCConnection` protocol.
Both sides apply `XPCPeerRequirement.isFromSameTeam(andMatchesSigningIdentifier:)` with the exact expected signing
identifier before activation. This is the verified public peer-authentication mechanism on the supported macOS 26
environment. `NSXPCConnection` does not expose the direct audit-token verification assumed by the earlier draft, so
no code may invent or privately fetch an audit token to satisfy that wording.

The XPC message protocol is closed and versioned. Gate 3 uses protocol V3 with exact, required XPC dictionary key/type

`updateConfiguration`, `configurationReadyToSwitch`, `configurationSwitchReady`, `configurationApplied`,

Wire slot IDs are only `0...2`; surface IDs are nonzero public 32-bit IOSurface IDs. Native Device requests require

screen with screen type `0`, display class `0`, and `isCarPlay == false`, then revalidates device and boot identity
before publishing bounded value identity. `SimDeviceScreen.isDefault` is observed and published truthfully but is not
an admission gate: the verified headless phone display returns `false`. It rejects missing/ambiguous server ports,
missing display ports, non-bijective/duplicate IDs, zero or multiple accepted screens, external/unknown/non-integrated screens, and
every identity change. It never selects by order, size, surface, or window state.

The exact locally verified ABI includes:

- `SimScreenAdapter.enumerateScreensWithCompletionQueue:completionHandler:`:
  static extended `v32@0:8@"NSObject<OS_dispatch_queue>"16@?<v@?@"NSArray"@"NSError">24` and runtime compact
  `v32@0:8@16@?24`;
- `SimScreen.registerScreenCallbacksWithUUID:callbackQueue:frameCallback:surfacesChangedCallback:propertiesChangedCallback:`:
  `v56@0:8@"NSUUID"16@"NSObject<OS_dispatch_queue>"24@?<v@?>32@?<v@?@"IOSurface"@"IOSurface">40@?<v@?@"<SimScreenProperties>">48`;

- `SimulatorKit.SimDeviceScreen.initWithDevice:screenID:`: `@28@0:8@16I24`, with `isDefault B16`,

- `SimDeviceIOPort`: `portIdentifier @16` and `descriptor @16`.

Terra must source-control the complete static encoding and check the exact compact `method_getTypeEncoding` result
before every invoked selector. The pinned binary identity authenticates extended metadata omitted by the compact
encoding. Gate 2 validates the future callback selector encoding but does not invoke it. Gate 2 performs no callback registration, frame delivery,
`framebufferSurface` access, or IOSurface work. Connection invalidation uses real idempotent per-session cleanup; the
Gate 2 implementation replaces Gate 1's earlier empty cancellation handler.

Because the screen/I/O protocols execute from CoreSimDeviceIO, Gate 2 adds its canonical nested framework executable
to the same pre-load, post-load, path, complete-resource-signature, bundle-version, Apple identifier/team, and exact
CDHash allowlist. Its signing identifier is `com.apple.CoreSimulator.CoreSimDeviceIO`, Team ID `59GAB85EFG`, bundle
versions `1051.17.8`, and canonical Security API CDHash
`8c83cde00a9609746fa819a3f3937e9db562ab29`.

The remote SimRenderServer remains CoreSimulator-owned. Gate 2 verifies its exact sealed on-disk service as
compatibility evidence before and after identity resolution: bundle identifier
`com.apple.CoreSimulator.SimRenderingServices.SimRenderServer`, Team ID `59GAB85EFG`, bundle versions `1051.17.8`,
and canonical Security API CDHash `78434a2124d3d00a2d5d8ad246cb93f62eabba2e`. The helper does not launch, attach to,
or claim peer authentication of that remote process, and it does not fetch an audit token. Runtime trust remains the
exact CoreSimulator/CoreSimDeviceIO path plus the returned exact framebuffer descriptor class, protocol surface,

Private Gate 2 invocation uses one helper-only Objective-C/Clang adapter target. It declares uniquely named local
calling protocols, validates Apple's real runtime protocols/classes and exact encodings before casting, and uses no

Core, CaptureCore, UI, and HTTPServer cannot import it.

Terra must record the exact screen-enumeration selector and every Objective-C type encoding from the installed Xcode
26.3 frameworks in the source-controlled adapter before calling them. The evidence above proves a buildable route; it
does not authorize serve-sim's largest-surface choice, callback retries, idle-frame replay, encoder, or network code.

The selected display must be proven as exactly one integrated/Internal non-CarPlay Simulator display and bound to its
exact screen identity. Rotation/dimension change advances a display-configuration generation only after the same screen identity is
proved. Missing, ambiguous, changed, or wrong device/display/generation clears the preview and fails closed.

The helper is supervised by the app but is not automatically restarted within a run. Crash, XPC invalidation,
identity violation, or protocol violation in `starting` fails the start. The same event in `recording` makes the run
incomplete while actions continue. Terminal transition, cancellation, app shutdown, and connection invalidation each
converge on one idempotent cleanup path. A new run may start a new helper only after old ownership is fully fenced.

### Fixed IOSurface ownership and bounded transport

Simulator-owned surfaces are recycled and never cross the helper boundary as stable owned frames.

For every accepted frame, the helper:

1. validates the raw surface against the exact device/display/generation;
2. locks it for read, records its IOSurface seed, and guarantees unlock on every exit;
3. copies it once into one safe slot in an exactly three-surface helper-owned IOSurface ring: `Fit Notch` uses one
   serial utility-QoS vImage aspect-fit into the exact positive-even tile dimensions, with black letterbox, no
   upscale, and preallocated scratch; `Native Device` copies the native BGRA rows into a native-sized slot and leaves

4. verifies the raw seed did not change and drops the candidate if it did;
5. transfers the helper-owned surface through the public IOSurface/XPC mechanism without another pixel copy; and
6. never reuses that ring slot until the app's explicit release acknowledgement arrives.

In steady state there is exactly one active K=3 ring and at most one outstanding newest-frame notification. A newer
eligible candidate replaces an older unsent candidate. If every active-ring slot is retained or busy, the helper drops
the new candidate. The active ring never grows and there is no per-frame task, queue, allocation, encode, log, or
backlog replay.

One in-flight `fitNotch <-> nativeDevice` setting update may allocate one bounded replacement K=3 staging ring while
the old K=3 ring remains active, for a hard maximum of six helper-owned destination IOSurfaces. The old mode stays
applied and displayed while all three staging surfaces, their public XPC objects, and any required vImage scratch are
allocated and validated. The staging ring receives no source frame and publishes no notification before commit. An
allocation or validation failure destroys the entire staging ring, leaves the old ring/generation/values healthy and
unchanged, and returns `UPDATE FAILED`.

After complete staging success, the helper fences new admissions, drops any unsent old candidate, drains the one copy,
and waits for exact release acknowledgements for old sent leases. It then atomically advances configuration and stream
generation, promotes the staging ring to the sole active K=3 ring, releases the old K=3 ring, proves active/staging
counts `3/0`, sends `configurationApplied`, and only then resumes new-generation admission. Old and new generations
never mix. Stop/cancel/finalizing can destroy staging and win at every suspension point.
FPS-only updates change the admission interval in place and allocate no surface or scratch memory.

Rotation/native-dimension callbacks use a separate closed `sourceReconfiguring` transaction. It outranks a setting
update, permanently cancels that update with `sourceConfigurationChanged`, destroys its staging resources, and proves
the old active K=3 before continuing. The helper fences admission/publication and sends `sourceReconfiguring` with a
helper-session-owned absolute continuous-clock release deadline. The app clears the preview, releases/acknowledges old
surfaces, and sends `sourceReleaseReady` only at zero mappings. Each display-configuration generation owns one
never-reused callback UUID and exactly one register/unregister pair. The adapter drains, unregisters, fences late
callbacks, and fully retires the old generation's exact UUID. It then destroys the old active K=3 ring and its scratch
before allocating replacement K=3 or creating/registering the new generation's UUID; automatic source reconfiguration
never uses K=6.

The helper then repeats the exact same-UDID, refreshed nonzero device-I/O boot generation,
screen-ID/unique-ID, integrated/Internal,
non-CarPlay, strict-BGRA, and dimension validation. It observes and republishes `isDefault` without gating on it. On
success it increments display-configuration and stream
generation, keeps the applied setting revision unchanged, publishes `sourceReconfigured` with latest sequence zero,
and waits for a real frame numbered one. Revalidation, release, drain, allocation, registration, or numeric-overflow
failure clears the preview and terminates the stream. It never resumes stale orientation, rebinds, chooses another
surface, or allocates a staging ring.

Every helper-originated post-start terminal path uses one release handshake:

```text
streamTerminating -> app clear/release -> terminalReleaseReady | terminal deadline -> helper cleanup
  -> streamStopped | streamFailed
```

Immediately before sending `streamTerminating`, the helper session queue records and sends one absolute deadline equal
to its current continuous clock plus exactly 2 seconds. It is the sole deadline/terminal owner. The app sends ready
only after all mapping/presentation/GPU ownership is gone. The helper then unregisters, drains once, releases every
active/staging resource, and sends one final result. No stop/cancel success is sent early. Race precedence is
`failure > cancel > stop`; terminal outranks source reconfiguration, which outranks a setting update. Terminal slots
are never reused. XPC invalidation needs no impossible acknowledgement or final reply; the helper fences,
unregisters/drains/releases once, and never reuses that session's slots.

The app-side transport actor retains/maps at most one current surface, rejects wrong or late identity/generation/
sequence, and acknowledges release when the UI replaces or clears it. Main-actor work is one preprocessed-surface swap
coalesced to display refresh. Callback and copy queues use utility QoS and remain below action work.

The first POC accepts only non-planar `kCVPixelFormatType_32BGRA` with four bytes per element and a safe row stride.
It does not silently convert `R10k`, `RGhA`, RGBA, planar, or unknown input. Fit Notch uses one serial
`vImageScale_ARGB8888` path whose scratch requirement is queried and allocated before callback registration. Native
Device uses row-by-row copy and never assumes equal source and destination row strides.

Maximum FPS is a callback-admission throttle, not a frame-production target. The helper admits at most one real
source callback every `66,666,667`, `33,333,334`, or `16,666,667` nanoseconds for 15, 30, or 60 FPS. It never sleeps
and later replays a callback, runs a duplication timer, repeats a static frame, or fabricates a frame to meet a rate.

### Preview settings and HUD truth

The Live Test Evidence Settings pane persists:

| Setting | Closed values | Fresh value |
|---|---|---|
| Private framebuffer consent | explicit Boolean | `false` |
| Preview size | `fitNotch`, `nativeDevice` | `fitNotch` |
| Maximum FPS | `15`, `30`, `60` | `30` |
| Destination | one validated standardized absolute directory | no silent fallback |

The fixed notch shows one exact-device identity, one live tile, stream health, preview-size/FPS controls, real matching

# ADR 0050: Use a Supervised Exact-UDID Simulator Framebuffer Helper and Record Only the Activity Notch

## Status

Accepted

## Date

2026-08-14

## Context

VisionCapture needs one phone-friendly visual record of a live Simulator test. The record must show the real selected
Simulator beside the real activity and proof rows already rendered in the activity notch. It must work when the
selected Simulator has a visible Simulator.app window and when Simulator.app shows no window for that device.

Public Apple tooling can take screenshots and record a device video, but it does not expose the required continuous
in-memory display stream. ScreenCaptureKit can record the VisionCapture notch window, but it cannot supply a
no-window Simulator framebuffer. The needed source is therefore a compatibility-sensitive private
CoreSimulator/SimulatorKit route.

This decision is hard to reverse because it creates a private-framework boundary, a bundled process, an XPC protocol,
a public MCP contract, persisted consent, a durable output shape, and release-package obligations. It would also be
surprising if future work moved private selectors into the main app, recorded a second Simulator file, silently
changed devices, or let preview work delay MCP actions.

The current branch contains the activity notch and its operation-ID proof merge. Gate 1's contained signed XPC helper,
closed transport/provenance checks, helper package resources, and assembly/probe seams are implemented and
source-approved. Gate 2's helper-only private adapter and exact-UDID integrated/Internal-display identity source gate are
also implemented and source-approved. Gate 2 live Simulator evidence is still pending and is not accepted at the
product gate.

The public live-test recording object, recording coordinator, exact-notch recorder, preview settings, Gate 3 frame
callback/IOSurface transport, preview UI, and notch-recording integration remain **planned, not implemented**.

ADRs 0045 through 0049 were accepted on the earlier recording branch but are not files in this branch. Their retained
rules are restated here so this ADR has no dangling local links. The frozen reference is recording-branch commit:

```text
e8c329db56f1429e43a7137cb463d34296506f3b
```

That earlier design recorded one notch video plus one Simulator video for every requested UDID. This decision replaces
that media shape and its multi-device recording model. It retains the useful lifecycle, wire separation, output
durability, privacy, performance-isolation, activity-pulse, and bounded-finalization rules where they are compatible
with one device and one video.

The owner-approved source specification is
[Single-Device Live Simulator in Recorded Notch](../active/live-notch-work/specification/spec-single-device-live-simulator-in-recorded-notch-2026-08-14.md).

## Decision

For one explicitly requested recording run, VisionCapture binds one immutable exact Simulator UDID, streams that
device's unique integrated/Internal non-CarPlay display through one supervised bundled XPC helper, renders the live
pixels inside the existing activity notch, and records only that exact notch window to one H.264 MP4.

The device stream is live in-memory presentation. It is not a source recording. The only pixel-bearing media output is:

```text
<run-directory>/notch__journey.mp4
```

There is no provider choice, replacement provider, retry/reconnect, device substitution, screenshot polling,
Simulator video, post-run merge, network stream, or fallback.

### Relationship to ADR 0024

[ADR 0024](./0024-use-mode-specific-execution-for-visible-and-headless-computer-use.md) remains accepted and
unchanged. It chooses input transport: exact-window input for visible Computer Use and the driver lane for headless
actions. This ADR chooses only the visual preview source and notch-recording path. Preview never selects an action
transport, never changes caller authority, and never changes WDA, proof, OCR, Accessibility, cache, or Interaction
Truth.

"No-window" means Simulator.app does not need to show or own a window for the selected device. A logged-in graphical
macOS session and WindowServer are still required because VisionCapture must render and record the notch.

### One immutable exact UDID

- `recording.command=start` accepts `udids` with exactly one non-empty exact Simulator UDID.
- Zero entries or more than one entry is malformed and rejects before a run ID or side effect.
- The trimmed UDID is copied into immutable run identity.
- The helper binds only that exact UDID. It never uses a device name, `booted`, the first device, the largest surface,
  or another convenient candidate.
- A second start while a run is non-terminal returns `RECORDING_CONFLICT`. It creates no run and leaks no active ID.
- Continue, stop, and cancel require the matching opaque recording ID.

### Public MCP recording contract V2

The current branch has no public recording wire. V2 is introduced selectively; it is not a runtime migration from a
shipped V1 on this branch.

VisionCapture keeps one public MCP tool, `execute`. It adds an optional closed top-level `recording` object:

```json
{
  "schema_version": 2,
  "command": "start | continue | stop | cancel",
  "recording_id": "<required canonical UUID for continue/stop/cancel>",
  "udids": ["<exactly-one-simulator-udid-for-start>"]
}
```

The retained request rules are:

- `start` requires `udids` and forbids `recording_id`.
- `continue`, `stop`, and `cancel` require `recording_id` and forbid `udids`.
- `start` and `continue` may accompany a normal operation. The normal operation's `parameters.udid` must equal the
  selected recording UDID.
- `stop` and `cancel` are allowed only on the control-only request `manage recording`.
- Control-only recording requests forbid `bundle_id`, `mode`, `parameters`, and `session_id`.
- The destination, helper, provider, preview size, and FPS never appear on the wire.
- Unknown fields, wrong types, unsupported schema versions, invalid command combinations, and zero/multiple UDIDs use
  JSON-RPC `-32602` before action IDs, proof events, device I/O, run allocation, helper launch, or file work.
- `RECORDING_UDIDS_REQUIRED` means a missing or empty start array.
- `RECORDING_UDID_INVALID` includes a non-string, blank, duplicate, or more-than-one start member.
- A normal-operation UDID mismatch uses `RECORDING_ACTION_UDID_MISMATCH` before either run or action side effects.
- When `recording` is omitted, response shape and action behaviour remain unchanged and no recording field is added.

A syntactically valid recording command result publishes one top-level `recording` object and one byte-equivalent
model-visible content block. Its `schema_version` is `2`. The retained fields are `command`, `accepted`, optional
`recording_id`, optional `state`, one-element `requested_udids`, `elapsed_ms`, `has_known_failure`, normal-branch
`paired_operation_started`, normal-branch `paired_operation_outcome`, optional `reason_code`, optional `message`,
optional `run_directory`, and terminal `videos`.

#### Amendment 2026-08-18 — `paired_operation_outcome` and the timeout code boundary

Additive V2 amendment. `schema_version` stays `2`; no field is removed, renamed, or given a new meaning.

`paired_operation_outcome` is **action status, not recording status**. It answers "did the paired normal operation
work?", which no recording field ever answered and which `accepted`, `state`, and `has_known_failure` must not be read
as answering.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `not_started` | The normal-operation pipeline was not entered. Always published with `paired_operation_started: false`. |
| `succeeded` | It was entered and the final action result has `isError != true`. Always with `paired_operation_started: true`. |
| `failed` | It was entered and the final action result has `isError == true`, whether from a thrown `ToolError`, another thrown error, or an error result returned normally. Always with `paired_operation_started: true`. |

The field is published on the normal branch (`start`, `continue`) and omitted on control-only `stop` and `cancel`,
exactly like `paired_operation_started`. Both fields are projections of one internal value, so they cannot disagree.

An ordinary action failure changes nothing on the recording half: it does not set `has_known_failure`, does not enter
recording `reason_code`, does not change recording `state`, and does not end the run. The two halves are independent
in both directions:

```json
{"isError": true,
 "recording": {"schema_version": 2, "accepted": true, "state": "recording",
               "has_known_failure": false,
               "paired_operation_started": true, "paired_operation_outcome": "failed"}}
```

```json
{"isError": false,
 "recording": {"schema_version": 2, "accepted": true, "state": "incomplete",
               "has_known_failure": true, "reason_code": "RECORDING_CHANNEL_FAILED",
               "paired_operation_started": true, "paired_operation_outcome": "succeeded"}}
```

Code boundary. The public identity of a failure is decided by **what failed**, never by which route carried it. Using
a managed route is not evidence about the frame channel.

| Code | Belongs to | Never used for |
|---|---|---|
| `SIMULATOR_UNRESPONSIVE` | An action/device operation exceeded its deadline, on the default route and the managed route alike. Carries `diagnosis` metadata: `device_not_ready` with `recovery_state: "preparing"` only when a read-only managed-set probe positively proved the cold-device condition; otherwise `probe_failed`, `service_unresponsive`, `device_unresponsive`, or `isolated_operation_timeout`. Readiness is never inferred from the timeout alone. | Recording transport failure. |
| `RECORDING_CHANNEL_FAILED` | An authoritative recording source/helper transport became terminal after the run entered `recording`. | Any `simctl`, WDA, app-lifecycle, accessibility, or device-service failure, and any timeout on a managed route. |
| `RECORDING_DEVICE_UNAVAILABLE` | Recording start preflight could not bind the requested device. | A failure after the run already entered. |
| `PROCESS_TIMEOUT` | Internal subprocess detail only. | Any public action identity. |

No new recording reason code is introduced for device readiness.

Terminal `videos` contains exactly one entry:

```json
{
  "kind": "notch",
  "status": "complete | partial | missing",
  "path": "<present only when the file exists>"
}
```

`kind: simulator`, a video-entry UDID, and a Simulator video path are invalid in V2. Recording state remains separate
from action/proof state. An accepted run may end `failed`, `incomplete`, or `cancelled` without rewriting the paired
action result. `askQuestion` remains present under ADR 0031 and never blocks the run.

Runtime rejections before a run are `RECORDING_CONFLICT`, `RECORDING_NOT_FOUND`, and
`SIMULATOR_STREAM_CONSENT_REQUIRED`. They use the existing MCP tool-result error envelope, set recording
`accepted: false`, and do not publish a guessed state or another run ID. A missing, false, or invalid stored consent
value maps only to `SIMULATOR_STREAM_CONSENT_REQUIRED` and has no side effect.

Accepted-run start failures use these public reason codes:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE` | Persisted destination is absent, invalid, unwritable, unsafe, or fails its durability probe. |
| `SIMULATOR_PREVIEW_SETTINGS_INVALID` | Persisted preview size or maximum FPS is absent from the closed allowed values. |
| `SIMULATOR_STREAM_UNSUPPORTED` | The exact host/Xcode/framework/private-adapter compatibility entry is not accepted. |
| `RECORDING_DEVICE_UNAVAILABLE` | The exact selected UDID is absent, not booted, or no longer matches the bound boot generation. |
| `SIMULATOR_DISPLAY_UNAVAILABLE` | The unique integrated/Internal non-CarPlay display or its identity is unavailable. |
| `SIMULATOR_PREVIEW_START_FAILED` | The selected display cannot deliver and present its first identity-valid frame. |
| `NOTCH_RECORDER_START_FAILED` | The exact notch window cannot be resolved or its writer cannot confirm recording. |
| `START_TIMED_OUT` | The one 30-second start budget expires. |

After state `recording`, source/helper loss uses public `RECORDING_CHANNEL_FAILED`, records bounded internal detail
`simulator_preview_lost`, clears the tile, shows `STREAM UNAVAILABLE`, and makes the run irreversibly incomplete.
`DEVICE_RECORDER_START_FAILED` is retired and must not be serialized by V2.

#### Amendment 2026-08-18b — explicit `launch app` verdict contract (`launch_outcome`), stage 1

Additive amendment. `schema_version` stays `2`, no recording field changes meaning, and every flat launch field
(`success`, `action`, `bundle_id`, `udid`, `device`, `already_running`, `pid`, `auto_recovery`) keeps its exact
current shape for compatibility.

Invariant: **a launch claim may exist only while fresh evidence created by that same request still proves it on the
exact route, UDID, and process instance at the response commit point.** A zero exit status from `simctl launch` is
not a launch claim, and a remembered attachment flag is not app liveness.

Every `launch app` response — success **and** failure — publishes one `launch_outcome` block. On success it sits in
the response payload and in the model-visible launch content block; on failure it travels in the error metadata and
is published at the tool-result root plus one model-visible content block.

```json
{"launch_outcome": {
  "verdict": "foreground_ready", "reason_code": null, "disposition": "attached",
  "mutation_sent": false, "requested_udid": "<caller-udid>", "bound_udid": "<route-proven-udid>",
  "route_kind": "default | managed", "device_readiness": "ready | not_ready | unproven",
  "boot_generation": "unproven",
  "process": {"state": "running | not_running | unproven", "bundle_id": "...", "pid": 1234,
              "start_identity": "unproven"},
  "foreground": {"state": "requested_app | other | system | unproven", "bundle_id": "...", "pid": 1234,
                 "evidence": "<source>"},
  "proof_age_ms": 18, "elapsed_ms": 842}}
```

A fact that was not proven is omitted or explicitly `unproven`. It is never filled from earlier state.
`mutation_sent` is `true`, `false`, or `"unknown"` — never a guessed `false`. `already_running` is only a projection
of `disposition: attached` and must never be read back as an input to a later decision.

| Verdict | Fresh evidence required | Public reason code |
|---|---|---|
| `foreground_ready` | Route revalidated, a fresh route-scoped process inventory proves the exact PID belongs to the requested bundle, and a fresh sessionless foreground read proves that same process is onscreen — all rechecked at commit. | none (success) |
| `running_not_foreground` | The requested process is freshly proven alive and a fresh foreground read proves another owner holds the screen. | `APP_RUNNING_NOT_FOREGROUND` |
| `crashed_on_launch` | A mutation was sent, a process was observed or launched, and exactly one new `.ips` report matches the bundle, the observed PID, the crash time window, and this exact Simulator device. | `APP_CRASHED_ON_LAUNCH` |
| `exited_during_launch` | A process was freshly observed after the command and then proven absent on the unchanged device, with no uniquely attributable report inside the window (`crash_report_status: not_found_within_window` or `ambiguous`). | `APP_EXITED_DURING_LAUNCH` |
| `not_running_after_launch` | A mutation was sent, no process was ever observed, and at least two final route-scoped inventories on the unchanged device prove zero matching processes. | `APP_NOT_RUNNING_AFTER_LAUNCH` |
| `not_attempted` | No mutation was submitted, and the exact preflight reason is known. `process.state` may claim `not_running` only when absence was positively proven. | `APP_NOT_INSTALLED`, `SIMULATOR_UNRESPONSIVE`, `SIMULATOR_ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE`, `LAUNCH_PRESTATE_NOT_PROVEN`, or the readiness code that refused |
| `outcome_unproven` | Route identity, process inventory, foreground identity, or the proof deadline prevented a trustworthy final state. `failed_proof_stage` names the exact stage. | `LAUNCH_OUTCOME_UNPROVEN`, or `LAUNCH_FAILED` / `LAUNCH_FOREGROUND_IDENTITY_MISMATCH` when that exact refusal is what failed |

`LAUNCH_FOREGROUND_NOT_PROVEN` is retired as a distinguishing code. It survives only as the legacy alias of
`outcome_unproven` and is published as `legacy_reason_code`, never as the public error identity.

Attach rule. "Already running" is proven at the attach commit, not remembered: the route is revalidated, a fresh
sessionless foreground read returns a positive PID, an independent route-scoped process inventory proves that exact
PID belongs to the requested bundle on that device, and route plus inventory are rechecked immediately before the
response commits. If attach proof is absent, fresh evidence proving the app is **not** running authorizes the single
`simctl launch`; a proven foreign foreground owner with a proven live process authorizes an activating launch;
anything else returns `not_attempted` with `LAUNCH_PRESTATE_NOT_PROVEN` — VisionCapture does not guess and does not
launch.

Crash detection is first-class. `AppLifecycleService` owns the deadline, the verdict, and the response; Interaction
supplies route-scoped process observations; a small injected host adapter snapshots and parses
`~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/*.ips`. The baseline is taken before the mutation, the drain is bounded and lives
inside the existing launch-proof deadline, and attribution requires **all** of: created or changed after the
baseline, requested bundle ID, matching observed or launched PID, crash time inside the window, exact Simulator
device attribution parsed from the crashed process path, and exactly one match. Two candidates produce
`exited_during_launch` or `outcome_unproven`, never a guess. A report that arrives after the response never rewrites
it. A dead PID is published as `last_observed_pid` and never in the live `process.pid` field.

Code boundary correction. Managed-route revalidation failure inside `runSimctl` no longer throws
`RECORDING_CHANNEL_FAILED`; it throws `SIMULATOR_ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE`, matching the boundary table above.

| Code | Belongs to | Never used for |
|---|---|---|
